name: Teach a dog sit, stay and come
blurb: Three cues that cover most of daily life with a dog. Modern training is reward-based and takes short, frequent sessions rather than long ones.
gear: A quiet space with no distractions to start
Patience and consistency across everyone in the household
steps: Learn the principle: reward the behaviour you want the instant it happens, and manage the environment so the wrong behaviour is hard.
Teach sit by luring with a treat over the nose so the back end drops, then mark and reward. Add the word only once the behaviour is reliable.
Teach stay by building duration first, then distance, then distraction — one at a time, never all three at once.
Teach recall as the most rewarding thing that ever happens: enormous rewards, every time, and never call them to something they dislike.
Keep sessions to a few minutes, several times a day, and end while it is still going well.
Generalise deliberately — a dog that sits in the kitchen has not learned to sit in the park.
tips: Never punish a dog that comes back to you, however long it took. It teaches them not to come next time.
Repeating a cue the dog is ignoring teaches them the cue means nothing. Go back a step instead.
Aversive methods carry real fallout risk. Reward-based training is both kinder and better evidenced.
proof: Your dog responds first time, in a distracting environment, off lead where it is safe and legal.
